title: OpenAI Report: AI Agents Now Complete Half of Researchers' Tasks on Their Own! 🔬
body: OpenAI Report: AI Agents Now Complete Half of Researchers' Tasks on Their Own! 🔬

OpenAI published yesterday its second report on the use of coding agents inside its research organisation, and the result was striking: agents now complete 46% of research tasks estimated to take two to four hours of human work, with no human intervention at all — up from 23% in March. For longer tasks of four to eight hours, the share rose from 13% to 35%.

"Coding agent" means software that writes and checks code on behalf of a researcher. A researcher's average daily use of agents reached about $2,400 at the published API prices, and the top 10% reached about $23,000 a day. In a survey, the median respondent said they would be willing to give up 40% of their team in exchange for keeping the agents for three months. But success varies by task — 79% for training monitoring, and only 25% for writing inference software — and humans are still at the centre of the work. And a note: the dollar figures are at the published API prices, not an actual bill, and these are the company's own measurements.
If AI were doing half your work.. would you fear for your job, or welcome the help? 💭
